name: Treaty of Sèvres, 1920
description: The peace treaty signed on 10 August 1920 between the Allies and the Ottoman government. It partitioned most of the empire, set up an independent Armenia and a referendum for Kurdistan, and gave Smyrna to Greek administration.
failedFuture: An Anatolia split between mandates, zones and small states, with a Kurdistan that might have existed. The Turkish national movement rejected the treaty and won the war; the borders were redrawn at Lausanne in 1923.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente atribuido vía Wikipedia (Bahçeli 2015, Erdoğan 2019, Le Monde 2020); los originales no se han consultado.

presentEffect.text: The 'Sèvres syndrome', the popular belief in Turkey that internal and external enemies conspire to carve up the republic, takes its name from the treaty. Devlet Bahçeli invoked it in 2015, Erdoğan said in 2019 'we overturned the Treaty of Sèvres', and Le Monde (31 July 2020) linked the opening of Hagia Sophia for worship to a 'new Treaty of Sèvres', which İbrahim Karagül answered in Yeni Şafak.

name: Anglo-French Union, 1940
description: The British offer of 16 June 1940 to France to merge the two countries into one "indissoluble" union, with a joint war cabinet, joint organs for defence, foreign and economic policy, and reciprocal citizenship.
failedFuture: Two nations that would have become one state in the middle of a collapse. The union stayed as a text, and the offer was never put into effect.
source: Anglo-French Declaration, 16 June 1940. Text at ibiblio.org (Policy Archive).
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente débil: el eco más reciente es de 2007. Verificado en Wikipedia.

presentEffect.text: The idea resurfaced in 1956, when Guy Mollet proposed a union with Elizabeth II as head of state and Anthony Eden rejected it. It became public through a BBC article by Mike Thomson on 15 January 2007, which coined the name 'Frangleterre'; on 16 January 2007 Charles Pasqua said on French television that a formal request would have led to Mollet being tried for high treason.

name: Gran Colombia, 1819-1831
description: The republic proclaimed in 1819 at the Congress of Angostura and shaped by the Constitution of Cúcuta (1821), covering present-day Colombia, mainland Ecuador, Panama and Venezuela.
failedFuture: Bolívar's union of the northern South American republics under one state. It broke into Venezuela, Ecuador and New Granada in 1830-1831; the source calls it 'the failure of Bolívar's vision'.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Sustituto verificado en Wikipedia. La propuesta de Chávez está marcada como 'reportedly' en la fuente.

presentEffect.text: The flags of Colombia, Venezuela and Ecuador share the tricolour of Gran Colombia's flag, and the name Colombia comes from this era. 'Unionistas' advocate reunification, and in 2008 Hugo Chávez reportedly proposed a political restoration of Gran Colombia.

name: Baruch Plan, 1946
description: The US proposal, presented by Bernard Baruch to the UN Atomic Energy Commission on 14 June 1946, to place nuclear material under an international authority, with sanctions that the Security Council could not veto.
failedFuture: A deal that would have given up the American monopoly on the bomb, if the Soviets accepted inspection in return. The Soviet Union refused, and the Baruch offer stayed on paper while the arms race started.
source: Baruch, B. (1946), UN Atomic Energy Commission. Wikipedia, "Baruch Plan".
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente atribuido (Bostrom 2014) vía Wikipedia; la ficha no vincula el plan con el OIEA ni con el TNP.

presentEffect.text: Wikipedia says the plan is often cited in works promoting the internationalisation of nuclear power or revisiting arms control, and Nick Bostrom cited it in Superintelligence (2014) as an example of how a power with a decisive strategic advantage might establish a benign 'singleton'.

name: Havana Charter and the International Trade Organization
description: The charter signed in Havana on 24 March 1948 to create the International Trade Organization, with rules on trade and on anti-competitive practices. The US government stopped seeking Senate approval in 1950.
failedFuture: A world trade body with its own rules, which was never created. The GATT took its place as a looser club, and the trade order of the postwar decades was built on that compromise.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente verificado en Wikipedia.

presentEffect.text: Elements of the Havana Charter became part of the GATT, which gradually became the main forum of trade cooperation. After the Uruguay Round of 1994 the World Trade Organization replaced the GATT in 1995 and adopted its principles and agreements.

name: European Defence Community, 1952–1954
description: The treaty signed on 27 May 1952 to create a single European army, under a common budget, within NATO. The French National Assembly ended its ratification in August 1954.
failedFuture: An army of Europe that would never be built. The French parliament postponed ratification indefinitely, and the idea of a common defence was shelved for decades.
source: Wikipedia, "Treaty establishing the European Defence Community".
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente atribuido vía Wikipedia; los hechos citados son posteriores a 2020. Año de concepción: 1950 (plan Pleven).

presentEffect.text: Wikipedia says the EU and NATO carry out some functions the EDC envisaged, though neither approaches its supranational military control. Federico Fabbrini (2024) and a 2025 study led by Sylvie Goulard argued that ratification remains legally feasible, and on 3 April 2025 Mauro Del Barba tabled a bill in the Italian Parliament to ratify the treaty.
presentEffect.source: Wikipedia, "Treaty establishing the European Defence Community" (citing Fabbrini, 2024; Goulard et al., 2025).

name: Stalin Note, 1952
description: The Soviet note of 10 March 1952 proposing a reunified, neutral Germany under a peace treaty, with the withdrawal of occupation forces within a year. The Western powers answered on 25 March 1952 by asking for free elections first.
failedFuture: A Germany that might have been neutral and whole, which the West refused. Adenauer chose integration into the Western alliance, and the division of Germany became permanent for another four decades.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente atribuido (debate historiográfico) vía Wikipedia; la ficha dice que el debate no intervino en la reunificación de 1990.

presentEffect.text: Historians still dispute whether a chance for a neutral, reunified Germany was missed. Rolf Steininger argued in 1985 that Stalin's offer was serious and that Adenauer blocked its testing; Hermann Graml argued the note was an alibi for integrating East Germany into the Eastern bloc. The debate recurred when Western archives opened in the 1980s and Eastern ones in the 1990s, with Zarusky's 2002 volume and Ruggenthaler's 2011 review.
presentEffect.source: Wikipedia, "Stalin Note" (citing Steininger, 1985; Graml; Zarusky, 2002; Ruggenthaler, 2011).

name: European Political Community, 1952–1954
description: The political community proposed in 1952 to bring the European Coal and Steel Community and the European Defence Community under one bicameral parliament and a supranational executive. It was abandoned in 1954, after the French National Assembly stalled the EDC.
failedFuture: A federal Europe that would have had a parliament before it had a constitution. It failed together with the defence treaty it was meant to crown.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente verificado en Wikipedia.

presentEffect.text: The ECSC assembly that drafted the treaty is now the European Parliament, so Wikipedia traces the Parliament's origins to this 1952 draft. Its failure redirected integration toward economic cooperation: the Messina Conference of 1955 led to the European Economic Community.

name: Federal Republic of Central America, 1823-1839
description: The federation created in 1823 from Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua, with a 1824 constitution drawing on the US federal model.
failedFuture: A united Central America. Civil wars broke out in 1827-1829 and 1838-1840, and Guatemala's Rafael Carrera decreed its dissolution in April 1839.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Sustituto verificado en Wikipedia; la ficha no describe las banderas ni el Parlamento Centroamericano.

presentEffect.text: All five former members belong to the Central American Integration System (SICA). Central American leaders have repeatedly called for reunification, but no attempt in the 19th or 20th centuries united all five states for more than a year.

name: Mali Federation, 1959–1960
description: A federation of French Sudan and Senegal, founded on 4 April 1959 within the French Community. Senegal left on 20 August 1960 and the federation dissolved after about four months.
failedFuture: An independent West African state that would have joined two former colonies in one country. It lasted barely a year and a half: two rival leaders and two armies ended it.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente verificado en Wikipedia; la ficha no recoge hechos posteriores a 1963.

presentEffect.text: The break-up left two states: the Sudanese Republic adopted the name Mali ('Le Mali Continue') and Senegal became independent. Keïta refused diplomatic relations with Senegal for years and Senghor became wary of unification projects; the Dakar–Niger railway reopened on 22 June 1963, when the two leaders met at the border.

name: United Arab Republic, 1958–1961
description: The union of Egypt and Syria, established on 1 February 1958. Syria left after a military coup on 28 September 1961; Egypt kept the name until 1971.
failedFuture: A single Arab state from the Nile to the Euphrates, which lasted three years. Pan-Arab unity remained a political idea after it, with no new state formed.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente verificado en Wikipedia.

presentEffect.text: Syria used the UAR's two-star flag from 1980 to 2024, and Iraq adopted a three-star flag in 1963 as a symbol of hoped-for unity. Egypt kept the name United Arab Republic until 1971, when it became the Arab Republic of Egypt.

name: West Indies Federation, 1958–1962
description: A federation of ten Caribbean territories, established in 1958, which collapsed in January 1962 after a 1961 referendum in Jamaica voted to leave.
failedFuture: A Caribbean nation of ten islands, under one parliament, that dissolved in four years. Jamaica's referendum split it in two, and the islands became independent one by one.
source: CARICOM, "The West Indies Federation". Wikipedia, "West Indies Federation".
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente verificado en Wikipedia.

presentEffect.text: The University of the West Indies grew out of the Jamaica campus. Successor bodies include CARICOM, the East Caribbean dollar and the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court (1981); the Caribbean Court of Justice is noted as a later body that could fulfil the role of the original federal court.

name: Kellogg-Briand Pact, 1928
description: Signed in Paris on 27 August 1928 and in effect from 24 July 1929, by which signatories renounced war as an instrument of national policy.
failedFuture: A world in which war was outlawed by treaty. It had no enforcement mechanism; many historians consider it largely ineffective, and Eric Sevareid called it a 'worthless piece of paper'.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Sustituto verificado en Wikipedia. Año de concepción: 1927 (negociación Kellogg-Briand), no confirmado en la ficha.

presentEffect.text: The pact remains in effect: Barbados (1971), Fiji (1973) and successor states of Czechoslovakia and Yugoslavia in the 1990s joined later. The Nuremberg and Tokyo tribunals used it as the basis of 'crimes against peace', and its central provisions were incorporated into Article 2(4) of the UN Charter. Hathaway and Shapiro argue it inaugurated 'a new era of human history'.

name: Sunningdale Agreement, 1973–1974
description: The December 1973 agreement at Sunningdale Park that created a power-sharing executive for Northern Ireland with a cross-border council. The Ulster Workers' Council strike of May 1974 brought the executive down on 28 May.
failedFuture: A Northern Ireland government shared between unionists and nationalists. A general strike of a few weeks ended it; the government had no will to use force against it, and the power-sharing idea waited two decades.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente verificado en Wikipedia; la frase de Mallon está atribuida.

presentEffect.text: Seamus Mallon, an SDLP negotiator, called the 1998 Good Friday Agreement 'Sunningdale for slow learners'; the political scientist Richard Wilford argues there are significant differences. Wikipedia says the present system of Northern Irish devolution is based on that agreement, and that Articles 2 and 3 of the Irish constitution, whose removal unionists demanded in 1973, were not revised until it.

name: New International Economic Order, 1974
description: The UN General Assembly declaration of 1 May 1974 calling for a New International Economic Order: fair prices for raw materials, technology transfer and sovereignty over natural resources for developing countries.
failedFuture: A world economy rebalanced for the countries that had been exporting raw materials for two centuries. Adopted by the UN; the debt crisis of the 1980s and the market turn made it impossible to realise.
source: UN General Assembly, Declaration on the Establishment of a New International Economic Order, A/RES/S-6/3201 (1974). Wikipedia, "New International Economic Order".
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente verificado en Wikipedia.

presentEffect.text: The Common Fund for Commodities came into force in 1989, one of the parts of the NIEO that were realised. A 2018 UN resolution, 'Towards a New International Economic Order', reaffirmed the need to keep working toward one, and Progressive International published updated proposals in September 2024.

name: Keynes's Bancor, 1940-1944
description: Keynes's proposed unit of account for an International Clearing Union, conceived between 1940 and 1942 and adopted as the UK's official proposal at the Bretton Woods Conference.
failedFuture: A postwar monetary order in which surpluses and deficits both carried penalties, so that countries would be pushed toward balanced trade. It was not accepted at Bretton Woods.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Sustituto: efecto atribuido (Zhou Xiaochuan 2009) vía Wikipedia; la ficha no menciona los DEG de 1969.

presentEffect.text: Zhou Xiaochuan, governor of the People's Bank of China, called Keynes's approach 'farsighted' in a 2009 speech and proposed IMF special drawing rights as a global reserve currency; US Treasury Secretary Timothy Geithner expressed interest, was heavily criticised, and the administration backtracked. A UN expert commission report (2009) and an IMF study (April 2010) made similar analyses.

name: Scandinavian Defence Union, 1948-1949
description: The 1948-1949 proposal for a defence alliance of Denmark, Norway and Sweden.
failedFuture: A neutral Nordic bloc with its own defence. Norway withdrew from the talks, Sweden saw few benefits and Finland could not join; the proposal collapsed.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Sustituto verificado en Wikipedia; parte de los hechos son posteriores a 2020.

presentEffect.text: NORDEFCO, an ad hoc Nordic defence cooperation body, was set up in 2009; in 2021 Denmark, Norway and Sweden agreed closer military coordination. Finland joined NATO on 4 April 2023 and Sweden on 7 March 2024, making all Nordic countries NATO members.

name: Meech Lake Accord, 1987–1990
description: A package of constitutional amendments agreed by Canada's first ministers at Meech Lake in 1987, recognising Quebec as a distinct society. Manitoba and Newfoundland did not ratify it before the June 1990 deadline.
failedFuture: A constitution that would have brought Quebec into the national compact. It lapsed in a single night in June 1990, when a legislator withheld consent and a premier judged the vote lost; the country's constitutional debate moved to a new round.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente verificado en Wikipedia; la fecha de fundación del Bloc (1990 o 15 de junio de 1991) es contradictoria en la fuente.

presentEffect.text: After the collapse, Lucien Bouchard, who had left Mulroney's cabinet in May 1990, led Quebec MPs who left their parties in forming the Bloc Québécois. The Bloc won 32 seats in the 2019 federal election, up from 10 in 2015, regaining official party status as the third-largest party in the House of Commons.

name: New Union Treaty, Soviet Union, 1991
description: The draft treaty for a new union of sovereign Soviet republics, due to be signed at Novo-Ogaryovo on 20 August 1991. The August coup stopped the signing; the treaty was never signed.
failedFuture: A Soviet Union that would have survived as a federation of sovereign states. The coup stopped the signature, and by December 1991 the union had dissolved by other means.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente verificado en Wikipedia; la ficha no recoge la Unión Económica Euroasiática.

presentEffect.text: The Commonwealth of Independent States was set up to replace the USSR with 12 newly independent states. The Baltic states never joined, Georgia joined in 1993 and withdrew in 2008 after the Russo-Georgian War, and Ukraine stopped participating in its statutory bodies in 2018.

name: Charlottetown Accord, 1992
description: A second package of constitutional reforms agreed in August 1992, covering Senate reform, Indigenous self-government and Quebec's distinct status. It was defeated in a national referendum on 26 October 1992.
failedFuture: A Canada that would have been redrawn through a vote of its own citizens. Voters across most provinces said no; the constitution stayed as it was, and the question of Quebec's place stayed open.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente verificado en Wikipedia.

presentEffect.text: Wikipedia says no further attempt to resolve Quebec's status through a formal constitutional process had been made as of 2025, and cites a Toronto Star headline describing the rejection as ending 'an era of constitutional reform'. The Québécois nation motion passed the House of Commons in 2006, the Clarity Act addressed Quebec's status through Parliament, and the Action démocratique du Québec was formed in 1994.

name: East African Federation, 1963-1964
description: In June 1963 Kenyatta, Nyerere and Obote met in Nairobi and agreed to aim for an East African Federation, to include Zanzibar, by the end of that year.
failedFuture: One East African state by the end of 1963. Uganda feared a subordinate role, Buganda wanted to keep its autonomy and the benefits were uneven; by late 1964 the plan had collapsed.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Sustituto verificado en Wikipedia.

presentEffect.text: The East African Community was established on 7 July 2000 and its common market launched in 2010. In 2017 Heads of State adopted a political confederation as a transitional step toward a federation, and a constitutional drafting committee was formed in 2018-2023; monetary union has been pushed back to 2031. Tanganyika and Zanzibar did unite in April 1964 to form Tanzania.

name: Vance–Owen Peace Plan, Bosnia, 1993
description: The 1993 plan by UN mediators Cyrus Vance and David Owen to divide Bosnia and Herzegovina into ten semi-autonomous provinces. The Bosnian Serb assembly rejected it, and a referendum followed.
failedFuture: A map of ten provinces that would have stopped a war. The Bosnian Serb side rejected it, and the war went on for two more years.
source: Wikipedia, "Peace plans proposed before and during the Bosnian War".
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente verificado en Wikipedia. La ficha habla de 'cantones'; el plan tenía diez regiones sin delimitar.

presentEffect.text: The Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina is divided into ten cantons, created by a law of 12 June 1996. Wikipedia says the cantons are the result of the Vance–Owen Peace Plan, which was applied only to part of the country; the plan had envisioned cantonisation of the whole.
presentEffect.source: Wikipedia, "Cantons of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina".

name: Oslo Accords, 1993-1999
description: The Oslo I Declaration of Principles (September 1993) and Oslo II (1995), which divided the West Bank into Areas A, B and C.
failedFuture: A five-year interim period leading to a permanent peace by May 1999. It ended without a final agreement; settlement expansion continued and the Second Intifada followed.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Sustituto verificado en Wikipedia.

presentEffect.text: The Palestinian Authority still exists. Area C covers about 60% of the West Bank and remains under Israeli control, with less than 1% of it designated for Palestinian use; Israel's Civil Administration and the Joint Water Committee still operate. In 2020 the PA suspended security coordination over planned annexations and restored it in November 2020.

name: Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty, 1996
description: The treaty signed on 24 September 1996 banning all nuclear explosions. It has not entered into force: nine further Annex 2 states must ratify it, including the United States, China and Russia.
failedFuture: A world in which no nuclear explosion would be tested, verified by a global network. Opened for signature on 24 September 1996, it has not entered into force: nine listed states have still to ratify it.
source: Arms Control Association, "Comprehensive Test-Ban Treaty (CTBT)". Wikipedia, "Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty".
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente verificado en la página de Arms Control Association (datos de 2024).

presentEffect.text: The treaty has still not entered into force: as of 2024, nine more states must ratify it (China, North Korea, Egypt, India, Iran, Israel, Pakistan, Russia and the United States, as the Arms Control Association lists them). The Preparatory Commission of the CTBTO and its International Monitoring System keep operating, and Article XIV conferences continue to meet.
presentEffect.source: Arms Control Association, "The Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty at a Glance".

name: Pan-Europa, Coudenhove-Kalergi's union
description: Richard von Coudenhove-Kalergi's manifesto Paneuropa (1923) began the Pan-European movement. Aristide Briand gave a widely recognised speech at the League of Nations in Geneva on 5 September 1929 calling for a federal Europe.
failedFuture: A federal Europe built from the Pan-European movement. Nazi Germany prohibited the organisation in 1933; it was refounded after the Second World War.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente verificado en Wikipedia. Cierre = prohibición nazi de 1933 (la unión fue refundada). La ficha no fecha el Picnic Paneuropeo.

presentEffect.text: The International Paneuropean Union, described as the oldest European unification movement, still exists, with its General Secretariat in Munich. It became known for organising the Pan-European Picnic during the Revolutions of 1989, and Otto von Habsburg was its international president from 1973.

name: UN Partition Plan for Palestine, 1947
description: On 29 November 1947 the UN General Assembly voted 33 to 13, with 10 abstentions, for Resolution 181: a plan to partition Mandatory Palestine into an Arab and a Jewish state, with an international regime for Jerusalem and an economic union.
failedFuture: Two states in Mandatory Palestine. The Arab Higher Committee, the Arab League and Arab governments rejected the plan; civil war broke out, the British Mandate ended on 14 May 1948, and the plan was not implemented.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente verificado en Wikipedia. La ficha no dice que la Declaración de Independencia de Israel cite la resolución.

presentEffect.text: The PLO's Palestinian Declaration of Independence (1988) relied on Resolution 181 as a basis for Palestinian sovereignty, and in a 2004 advisory opinion the International Court of Justice cited the Palestinian people's entitlement to a state 'as originally envisaged in Resolution 181 (II)'. 29 November is the International Day of Solidarity with the Palestinian People.

name: Camp David Summit, 2000
description: The summit at Camp David from 11 to 25 July 2000, hosted by Bill Clinton, between Ehud Barak and Yasser Arafat. It left Jerusalem, refugees and borders unresolved, and ended without agreement.
failedFuture: A two-state peace that was almost signed. The summit broke over Jerusalem and the refugees.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente atribuido vía Wikipedia (Malley, Swisher, Finkelstein, Ben-Ami); los originales no se han consultado.

presentEffect.text: The 'generous offer' story, that Israel offered a state on about 91% of the West Bank and Gaza and Arafat refused, is still contested: Robert Malley, Clayton Swisher and Norman Finkelstein challenged it, and Shlomo Ben-Ami said in 2006 that Camp David was not the Palestinians' missed opportunity. Israeli analysts argue the narrative weakened the Israeli peace movement.

name: Kyoto Protocol, 1997–2001
description: The 1997 protocol that set binding emission targets for developed countries. The United States signed it in 1998 but never submitted it to the Senate, and President Bush opposed it in March 2001. It entered into force in 2005.
failedFuture: A binding climate agreement that the world's largest economy never ratified. Its first commitment period ended in 2012, leaving a framework without the American target.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente verificado en Wikipedia.

presentEffect.text: The Doha Amendment, extending the protocol to 2020, entered into force on 31 December 2020, the day the second period ended. The Clean Development Mechanism and the EU Emissions Trading System, which drove about 97% of international carbon market trade in 2010, descend from it. The US signed in 1998 and never ratified; the Paris Agreement of 2015 succeeded it after 2020 as a separate instrument.

name: Annan Plan, Cyprus, 2004
description: The UN plan for the reunification of Cyprus as a federation, put to simultaneous referendums on 24 April 2004. The Turkish Cypriot vote approved it, the Greek Cypriot vote rejected it.
failedFuture: A single island with two communities and one federal state, ready the day Cyprus entered the European Union. Greek Cypriots said no by three votes in four, and the island joined the EU divided.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente verificado en Wikipedia (fuente antigua, con referencias de 2014-2015). Año de concepción: 2004 (referendos); el plan se presentó antes (pendiente de confirmar).

presentEffect.text: Because the plan failed, EU law remains suspended in the areas outside government control under Protocol 10 of the 2003 Accession Treaty, while Turkish Cypriots keep EU citizenship as citizens of the Republic of Cyprus. The source describes the island as divided since 1974.

name: Free Trade Area of the Americas, 1994–2005
description: The proposed trade agreement among 34 countries of the Americas, launched in Miami in 1994 and due by 2005. Negotiations ended without agreement at the Mar del Plata summit in November 2005.
failedFuture: A single market from Alaska to Tierra del Fuego, with no tariffs between its members. The talks broke over farm subsidies and intellectual property; the continent went on trading in pieces.
source: Wikipedia, "Free Trade Area of the Americas". CRS, "A Free Trade Area of the Americas" (2005).
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente verificado en Wikipedia.

presentEffect.text: The US built a patchwork instead: NAFTA was superseded by the USMCA in 2020, and DR-CAFTA (2008) and bilateral deals with Chile (2004), Peru (2007), Colombia (2011) and Panama (2011) followed, along with the Pacific Alliance (2012). Hugo Chávez promoted ALBA as a counterproposal, calling the FTAA an 'annexation plan'.
presentEffect.source: Wikipedia, "Free Trade Area of the Americas".

name: Treaty establishing a Constitution for Europe, 2004–2005
description: The constitutional treaty of the European Union, signed in Rome on 29 October 2004. It was rejected in referendums in France (29 May 2005) and the Netherlands (1 June 2005).
failedFuture: A European constitution that a continent did not want. Two referendums closed its ratification, and the Lisbon Treaty replaced it with a less visible text.
source: Wikipedia, "Treaty establishing a Constitution for Europe".
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente verificado en Wikipedia.

presentEffect.text: The Treaty of Lisbon, in force since 1 December 2009, carried over many of its changes, adopted its amendment procedures and an identical exit clause, and 'abandoned the idea of a single codified constitution'.
presentEffect.source: Wikipedia, "Treaty establishing a Constitution for Europe".

name: Doha Development Round, 2001–2006
description: The World Trade Organization round launched in Doha in November 2001 to reduce trade barriers, especially on agriculture. It was suspended at the end of July 2006.
failedFuture: A trade round that would have served the developing world, suspended with no conclusion. The disagreement over agriculture remained the central obstacle when talks resumed.
source: Europeansources.info, "The WTO Doha Development Round: Where next for world trade?".
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente verificado en Wikipedia. La fuente original de la ficha (2006) no cubre este efecto.

presentEffect.text: The Bali Package of December 2013, the first WTO agreement approved by all members, forms part of the Doha Round. Its Trade Facilitation Agreement entered into force on 22 February 2017, and the Peterson Institute estimated it could generate US$1 trillion in economic activity.

name: Ahtisaari Plan, Kosovo, 2007
description: The UN special envoy Martti Ahtisaari's proposal for the future status of Kosovo, sent to the UN Secretary-General in March 2007. It provided for a wide degree of self-government and an international supervision, without using the word independence.
failedFuture: A status for Kosovo that avoided the word independence while providing for much of a state. Serbia called it illegitimate and unacceptable, and the Security Council never adopted it.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente verificado en Wikipedia; la ficha acaba en 2012.

presentEffect.text: On 10 September 2012 the International Steering Group ended its supervision, and Kosovo's constitution became the sole basis of its legal framework, no longer subordinate to the Comprehensive Status Proposal. In 2012 Serbia's president Tadić proposed a Five-Point Plan, described as a reworking of the Ahtisaari Plan.

name: Copenhagen Accord, 2009
description: The climate accord of 18 December 2009 at the COP15 in Copenhagen, which recognised the goal of limiting warming to 2 °C. It was not legally binding; delegates only took note of it.
failedFuture: A climate treaty that would have set the world on a path below 2 °C. Delegates at COP 15 only 'took note of' a non-binding accord drafted by the United States and the BASIC countries, and no decision was made on a legally binding successor to Kyoto.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente verificado en Wikipedia; la ficha no vincula el acuerdo con Cancún ni París.

presentEffect.text: The accord recognised that warming should stay below 2 °C and set a goal of raising $100 billion per year by 2020. National pledges targeted 2020, among them the EU at 20–30% below 1990 levels, the US at 17% below 2005 and China at 40–45% lower carbon intensity than 2005; a UNEP assessment of November 2010 identified an 'emissions gap'.

name: Chequers plan, 2018
description: The UK government's Brexit proposal agreed at Chequers on 6 July 2018, a close economic relationship with the EU through a common rulebook for goods. Davis and Johnson resigned in July 2018, and the EU rejected the plan in September 2018.
failedFuture: A Brexit that kept the UK inside the single market for goods, and was judged unworkable by the other side. It did not survive; its idea of frictionless trade survived in the Political Declaration of November 2018.
license: Pendiente: verificar licencia de la imagen
status: Efecto presente débil pero verificado en Wikipedia; la ficha no cubre el Acuerdo de Comercio y Cooperación de 2020.

presentEffect.text: Its common-rulebook idea carried into the Political Declaration of 25 November 2018, which Wikipedia calls 'the centrepiece of the Chequers plan'. The facilitated customs arrangement aimed to avoid a hard border on the island of Ireland, and the resignations of David Davis and Boris Johnson in July 2018 marked a major government crisis.
